query: Which clinical factors best explain longer visit durations?

per_column.name: procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: A binary procedure/order flag is a plausible driver of visit duration and gives a real grouping axis. Grounding is mixed: labs ordered (row1) and MRI ordered (row5) reasonably count as procedures/orders, but the MI follow-up (row3) marked 1 has only an echo referenced as a past result, and the URI visit is 0, which is defensible. Some values stretch 'procedure performed' vs 'ordered'.

per_column.name: chronic_condition_count
per_column.rationale: Chronic condition burden is a genuine clinical factor likely correlated with duration. Values look sound: post-MI on statin/beta-blocker = 1, acute URI/knee injury/acne/physical = 0. Reasonable readings of the text.

per_column.name: systems_involved_count
per_column.rationale: Case complexity via organ-system count is a useful modeling axis. However some counts are questionable: the annual physical (row1) marked 4 seems inflated for a routine exam, and acne (row4) marked 2 is generous. Extraction is inconsistent and partly unsupported by the text.

per_column.name: referral_or_consult
per_column.rationale: Referral/consult is a distinct workflow factor that plausibly lengthens visits. All five samples are 0, which is consistent with the source texts (none mention a referral/consult), so grounding is sound though variance is low in the sample.

per_column.name: medication_mentions
per_column.rationale: Medication-related complexity is a reasonable axis. Values are well grounded: acne row correctly 1 (adapalene/doxycycline as new meds), URI 0. The MI follow-up scored 0 despite beta-blocker/statin is arguably a definitional choice (new vs continued meds), still defensible.

per_column.name: note_word_count
per_column.rationale: Raw word count is a generic surface feature with little clinical explanatory leverage for the query and is near-constant (18-30, tightly clustered). Values are trivially derivable and accurate, but analytical value is low.

judge.rationale: Most added columns supply genuine clinical axes (procedures/orders, chronic burden, case complexity, referrals, medications) that plausibly explain visit duration and enable grouping/modeling. Groundedness is generally acceptable but weakened by inflated systems_involved_count values (e.g. 4 systems for an annual physical) and some liberal readings of 'procedure performed'. note_word_count is well grounded but adds little analytical leverage for this query, dragging the holistic usefulness down.
